items.claim: The front seam at 26:7 is argued as a clean turn to public narration, but two byte-true devices inside the span reach back across that seam undisclosed, and the boundary is still rated high confidence.
items.evidence: The seizure notice defines itself by the pre-seam material: 26:8 opens its completion clause אֵ֣ת כָּל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה לְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל כָּל הָעָ֑ם (oshb:Jer.26.8, byte tier), which resumes the divine charge given two verses before the seam, אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖יךָ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.26.2, byte tier). 26:9 then quotes the pre-seam threat back, כְּשִׁלוֹ֙ יִֽהְיֶה֙ הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.9, byte tier), against אֶת הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה כְּשִׁלֹ֑ה (oshb:Jer.26.6, byte tier) — and the two Shiloh forms differ by site, כְּשִׁלוֹ֙ (oshb:Jer.26.9, byte tier) against כְּשִׁלֹ֑ה (oshb:Jer.26.6, byte tier), a per-site spelling pair the span straddles without a word. Both devices argue continuity with the commissioning scene across the row's own opening and neither is disclosed; the only disclosure offered at the seam is the setumah at MT 26:6, single-witness and weak in the Prophets, which cannot carry a boundary. The Hebrew engagement offered for the seam itself is a scene-shift verb, and the same verb shape opens the next seam at 26:10, so it does not discriminate between the two cuts. High confidence is not supported while the cross-seam anaphora stands unaddressed.
tier_citations: parashah setumah at MT 26:6 (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets)

items.claim: The closure argument rests on an untiered verbatim-class recurrence claim that the bytes contest: accusation and acquittal share a collocation but neither an order nor an accentuation.
items.evidence: The row says the acquittal answers the charge in the very words used to accuse, with no tier named. The bytes give מִשְׁפַּט מָ֨וֶת֙ לָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.11, byte tier) against אֵין לָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ מִשְׁפַּט מָ֔וֶת (oshb:Jer.26.16, byte tier): the same four-word set, but reordered around the negator, and each of the three accented words carries a different accent in the two verses, visible in the two splices themselves at byte tier. The recurrence is real at skeleton tier and not at byte tier, and the label the campaign requires for a verbatim-class claim is absent. The digit that would have carried the point is also missing: the two-word death-sentence collocation is confined to these two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses), both inside this span — an exclusivity available to the row and unclaimed. Mark disclosure in this row is exact: the setumah at MT 26:10 at its own opening and the setumah at MT 26:15 inside the span both check out, single-witness and correctly typed.
tier_citations: parashah setumah at MT 26:10 and MT 26:15 (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets)

items.claim: Both original-language disclosures overstate what the bytes give: the qere is reported one word too wide, and the plene contrast is drawn against a comparand that does not isolate the plene variable.
items.evidence: MT 26:18 carries one ketiv/qere note in the single-witness inventory, and the verse bytes open with the unpointed ketiv מיכיה followed by the pointed qere מִיכָה֙ (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier) — one word. The row reports the qere as a two-word phrase that also takes in הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier), which is ordinary text outside the note: the note's extent and the reported extent are not the same, in exactly the verse where a slicing claim owes the note a careful reading. Second, the plene form at this site is וִירוּשָׁלַ֨יִם֙ (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier), vav-prefixed; the row contrasts it with יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ (oshb:Jer.25.18, byte tier), which is not vav-prefixed, so the pair differs in two respects at once and does not isolate the mater the claim is about. A same-shape defective comparand exists (sweep: 6 verses for the vav-prefixed defective spelling), including וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Jer.27.21, byte tier). The plene spelling itself is a single site book-wide (sweep: 1 verse), which is the digit the contrast wanted. The parashah statement for the span is correct: no marked verse falls in 26:17-19 and MT 26:16 is unmarked.
tier_citations: ketiv/qere note at MT 26:18 (single-witness inventory, one note)
skeleton tier sweep: 1 verse (plene spelling), 6 verses (vav-prefixed defective spelling)

items.claim: Each of the row's two argumentative pivots turns on a particle it does not weigh: the opening coordinator is byte evidence for the reading the row rejects, and the closing adversative that carries the asserted contrast is left outside the splice.
items.evidence: 26:20 opens וְגַם אִ֗ישׁ הָיָ֤ה מִתְנַבֵּא֙ (oshb:Jer.26.20, byte tier). The row splices the coordinator and then reads the verse as standing on its own footing rather than continuing the elders' speech, without weighing that the coordinator is itself the byte ground for the continuation reading it sets aside; no counter-evidence in the bytes is offered against it. At the other end the contrast claim rests on 26:24, whose bytes open אַ֗ךְ יַ֚ד אֲחִיקָ֣ם (oshb:Jer.26.24, byte tier); the row's splice begins at the second word and drops the adversative, so the one particle that marks the contrast between Uriah's execution and Jeremiah's protection is the word excluded from the row's own quotation, while the English rendering beside it reaches wider than the splice does. The petuchah disclosed at MT 26:24 checks out, single-witness and correctly typed, and the disclosure is complete for the span: across MT 26:20-26:24 the inventories carry 1 mark, 0 paseq segs and 0 ketiv/qere notes.
tier_citations: parashah petuchah at MT 26:24 (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets)

items.claim: The stated ground for holding 27:1-11 together is byte-refuted — the row denies any fresh discourse imperative in verses 5 through 10, and 27:9 carries one — and the closure signal in the row's own last verse goes unquoted.
items.evidence: The row asserts that nothing inside verses 5 through 10 reopens the message with a different speaker, an addressee change, or a fresh discourse imperative. 27:9 reads וְ֠אַתֶּם אַל תִּשְׁמְע֨וּ אֶל נְבִיאֵיכֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.27.9, byte tier) — a fronted second-person plural pronoun with a negative imperative, the discourse-frame shape this chapter uses four times (sweep: 6 verses book-wide for the imperative, four of them in this chapter, at 27:9, 27:14, 27:16 and 27:17). The unit may still hold, but not on the ground stated. The row's own closing verse carries נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.27.11, byte tier) and the splice stops immediately before it, passing up the closure corroboration standing at its own seam; the same verse's remainder, וְהִנַּחְתִּ֤יו עַל אַדְמָתוֹ֙ (oshb:Jer.27.11, byte tier), is rendered in the English gloss although it lies outside the splice. Two further gloss-beyond-splice sites: the header splice at 27:1 is glossed with the whole verse including the word-arrival clause, and the 27:3 splice is glossed with an arrival phrase it does not contain, הַבָּאִ֣ים יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.27.3, byte tier). The pre-seam close at 27:10, כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖ם נִבְּאִ֣ים לָכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.27.10, byte tier), also recurs past the seam at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses for this clause), undisclosed. The held-open royal-name crux is handled correctly and the bytes back it: the defective form stands at this site alone (sweep: 1 verse) against the full spelling elsewhere (sweep: 22 verses), and the construction בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלֶ֛כֶת יְהוֹיָקִ֥ם (oshb:Jer.27.1, byte tier) is verse-initial as the row treats it.
tier_citations: skeleton tier sweep: 6 verses (negative-listening imperative), 3 verses (false-prophecy clause), 1 verse (defective royal name), 22 verses (full royal name)

items.claim: The addressee turn anchoring this seam is byte-true, but a two-device refrain straddles the seam undisclosed and the ruled closure signal inside the row's own final verse is neither quoted nor listed.
items.evidence: The boundary itself is defensible: the addressee turns at both ends are verse-initial and byte-true, and the row's statement that no marked verse or note falls at the front seam, the interior or the end verse checks out: across MT 27:11-27:15 the inventories carry 0 marks, 0 paseq segs and 0 ketiv/qere notes. What is not disclosed is that the span's interior verse and the verse immediately past the seam carry the same two devices in near-identical form: וְאַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י הַנְּבִאִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.27.14, byte tier) against אַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י נְבִֽיאֵיכֶ֗ם (oshb:Jer.27.16, byte tier), and כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖ם נִבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.27.14, byte tier) against כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖מָּה נִבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.27.16, byte tier) — the same clause with only the pronoun byform varying (sweep: 3 verses for the shorter pronoun form, 1 verse for the longer byform). 27:14 is the one verse of the span the prose leaves unengaged, and it is the verse carrying both devices; a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity unless it is disclosed. The row's closing verse also opens כִּ֣י לֹ֤א שְׁלַחְתִּים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.27.15, byte tier); the splice begins after the formula, so the closure corroboration in the row's own last verse is absent from both the quotation and the declared signals.
tier_citations: skeleton tier sweep: 3 verses (shorter pronoun form of the false-prophecy clause), 1 verse (longer byform)
marked-verse and note inventories: no entry at MT 27:11-27:15 (single-witness)

items.claim: The declared speech-formula signal names an object that is not the one at the row's own onset, and three distinct formula shapes inside the span are carried under that single label, including the book's full divine stack at 27:21, which is never named.
items.evidence: The onset splice the row itself supplies reads כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.27.16, byte tier) — bare, without tsevaot — while the signal declared for the span names the tsevaot formula, so the label does not match the byte form at the seam it is attached to. Inside the span the shape changes twice more: כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.27.19, byte tier), and then כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.27.21, byte tier), which is the book's full divine stack and a count object of its own (sweep: 32 verses for the stack book-wide, 31 of them with the koh-amar opener). The row's rejected alternative names the clause at 27:19 as the second and stops; the third is nowhere disclosed, and it is the one of the span's 3 koh-amar sites that carries the full stack. The continuity conclusion is stated as though no koh-amar shape reopens inside the span. Speaker and addressee may well run on, but three formula objects are being blended under one key. The frame ownership is otherwise stated correctly and the mark disclosure here is complete and correctly typed: the petuchah at MT 27:18, the setumah at MT 27:20 and the closing petuchah at MT 27:22 are all present as claimed, and the paseq is at MT 27:18 as claimed, cited count-only.
tier_citations: skeleton tier sweep: 32 verses (full divine stack), 31 verses (stack with the koh-amar opener)
parashah petuchah at MT 27:18 and MT 27:22, setumah at MT 27:20 (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets)

items.claim: The row names the mouth for the opening divine formula but leaves the second divine formula in the same quoted speech unattributed while rendering it in English, and it labels a mid-verse dated construction with an onset key.
items.evidence: The attribution work on כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Jer.28.2, byte tier) is done properly and is the right instinct. The row's own closing verse then carries a second divine formula inside that same quoted speech, נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.28.4, byte tier); the splice stops well before it while the English rendering beside the splice reaches past it and renders it, so the formula is reported without the mouth-attribution the row insists on for the first one — and the false-prophet speech turns out to carry both the opening and the closing divine formulas, which is the sharper fact and goes unstated. That formula is also the closure corroboration standing at this row's own seam and is absent from the declared signals. Second, the declared date signal is an onset key, but at this site the construction is mid-verse and the row's own splice shows it: וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא בְּרֵאשִׁית֙ מַמְלֶ֨כֶת֙ (oshb:Jer.28.1, byte tier), third word in, against the verse-initial בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלֶ֛כֶת יְהוֹיָקִ֥ם (oshb:Jer.27.1, byte tier) carrying the same key; of the three sites of this construction (sweep: 3 verses), this is the one that is not verse-initial, and the position difference is flattened by the shared label. The ketiv/qere report is correct and byte-checkable: the note sits on the year phrase, unpointed ketiv against the pointed qere בַּשָּׁנָה֙ (oshb:Jer.28.1, byte tier), matching the single note the inventory carries at that verse; the petuchah at MT 27:22 before the opening also checks out.
tier_citations: ketiv/qere note at MT 28:1 (single-witness inventory, one note)
parashah petuchah at MT 27:22 (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets)
